title: Evangelical equity: precise duty to quit mortal sins; not to live without every lightest fault
source_text: XLI. Unde colligit fideles, etiam secundum epieikeian Evangelicam, stricte & praecise, sub periculo aeternae mortis obligari ad vivendum sine omnibus illis peccatis, quae mortalia vocantur. Quoniam ad perfectionem partium attinet, ut non solum de peccatis illis gravioribus poenitentiam agamus, sed etiam ut ab iis omnino abstineamus, hoc est, ut in posterum ea non committamus; juxta illud Christi, Ecce sanus factus es, ne pecca amplius. At non sic obligari, ut vivant in posterum sine omni peccato, etiam levissimo. Quoniam vivere sine levioribus illis peccatis, quae venialia vocantur, pertinet ad per-fectionem graduum, quae omnes obedientiae humanae naevos & defectus excludit.
pass_a_gloss: Whence he gathers that the faithful, even according to evangelical equity, are bound strictly and precisely under peril of eternal death to living without all those sins which are called mortal. Since it belongs to the perfection of parts that we not only repent of those heavier sins but also altogether abstain from them—that is, that thereafter we not commit them; according to that word of Christ, Behold you have been made whole; sin no more. But they are not so bound that they live thereafter without every sin, even the lightest. Since to live without those lighter sins which are called venial belongs to the perfection of degrees, which excludes all blemishes and defects of human obedience.
pass_b_english: Even under gospel equity: quit ‘mortal’ sins in act—repent and stay clear (John 5:14).
Living without every lightest ‘venial’ slip is degrees-perfection, not the precise life-condition.

choices.why: Mortal-class abstinence remains exact under gospel equity.
